1.

We have heard Ms. Kharkar, learned counsel for the petitioners and Dr. Birendra Saraf, learned Advocate General on the backdrop of earlier orders 08 August, 2024 5-WP 6330-21@IA 10095-24@WP 3394-19.DOC passed by us.

2. The issue in the present proceedings concerns the State Government taking appropriate steps to notify the Maharashtra Land Acquisition and Settlement Authority in terms of Section 51 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation and Resettlement) Act, 2013.

entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation and Resettlement) Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Dr. Saraf has placed on record figures of pendency of the proceedings before Nashik and Amravati Bench which is '1586' and '21109' respectively.

He has also placed on record a statement in regard to the pendency of the proceedings before Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar, Konkan, Pune and Nashik Division which is totalling to about '9445'.
4.

Dr. Saraf has submitted that as observed by this Court in the previous orders, a decision has been taken and the State Government is in the process of issuing a notification declaring two additional authorities, i.e., for Amravati and Nashik Division.
He states that Nashik authority would also be having jurisdiction in regard to Pune and Konkan Division and Amravati Divisional Authority in respect of Amravati, Akola, Buldhana, Yawatmal and Washim.

Thus, according to Dr. Saraf, there would be four authorities which would be functional namely one for Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar which is already functioning, second for Nagpur Division which is also presently functioning 08 August, 2024 5-WP 6330-21@IA 10095-24@WP 3394-19.DOC and two additional authorities for Amravati and Nashik (Konkan and Pune Division including).
5.
We are of the opinion that let such notification, which is in the process of being issued, be placed on record on the adjourned date of hearing.

Learned counsel for the petitioners, however, submits that pendency of the proceedings before Konkan, Pune and Nashik Division is quite large, as also it may not be convenient for the litigants of Konkan to travel all the way to Nashik, as also the litigants from Pune Division to Nashik in regard to adjudication of their cases as already meager amount of compensation is being paid.
It is submitted that this would be causing prejudice to large number of litigants to travel all the way to Nashik for adjudication of their reference proceedings.

We are of the opinion that the contention as urged on behalf of the petitioners definitely is a valid contention,
which may be required to be taken into consideration by the State Government, however, we do not intend to pass any order on this as on date, as we are awaiting the notification to be issued by the State Government.
We shall consider all the other contentions in the proceedings on the adjourned date of hearing.

6. Stand over to 16 August, 2024 (H.O.B.).
7.
Ad-interim order passed earlier shall continue to operate till the adjourned date of hearing.
